name: Elhanan
interpretive_note: 2 Samuel 21:19 states that Elhanan the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite, appearing to conflict with 1 Samuel 17, where David kills Goliath. 1 Chronicles 20:5 records instead that Elhanan killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath. Evangelical scholars are divided on how to resolve this: some regard 1 Chronicles 20:5 as preserving the more original and accurate text, with a copying difficulty in 2 Samuel 21:19 having dropped or altered a word; others suggest "Goliath" in 2 Samuel 21:19 was a title or name shared by more than one Philistine champion. Scripture does not resolve the question itself, so no single explanation is presented here as certain.
source_summary: One of David's mighty men from Bethlehem who killed a Philistine giant in battle, described in 2 Samuel 21:19 as Goliath the Gittite and in 1 Chronicles 20:5 as Goliath's brother Lahmi.
family_friendly_summary: Elhanan was one of King David's brave warriors, and he came from the same town as David: Bethlehem. During a war against the Philistines, Elhanan defeated one of their fearsome giant warriors in battle, a relative of the famous giant Goliath. The Bible tells this story in two slightly different ways in two different books, and people have wondered for a long time exactly how the details fit together. What's clear either way is that Elhanan was a courageous fighter who helped defend Israel against giants during David's reign, alongside the other mighty men who served the king faithfully.
adult_story: Elhanan, son of Dodo of Bethlehem (called Jair in 1 Chronicles 20:5), was one of David's mighty men and is remembered for killing a Philistine giant, "the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam" (2 Samuel 21:19; 1 Chronicles 20:5). The two accounts differ in an important detail: 2 Samuel 21:19 names Elhanan's opponent as "Goliath the Gittite," the same name given to the giant David famously killed in 1 Samuel 17, while the parallel account in 1 Chronicles 20:5 names the opponent as "Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite." This is one of the more well-known text-critical questions in the Old Testament, and Scripture itself does not explain the discrepancy (see interpretive note). What is not in dispute is Elhanan's inclusion among David's elite warriors, listed by name alongside Bethlehem's other mighty men in the roster of 2 Samuel 23:24 and 1 Chronicles 11:26. Whichever giant he faced, Elhanan's account continues a larger pattern in these chapters: after David's own victory over Goliath, several more of his mighty men went on to strike down other Philistine giants, including a massive warrior with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, and "these were born to the giant in Gath" (2 Samuel 21:15-22). Elhanan's courage under fire was part of Israel's broader victory over the Philistine threat during David's reign.
devotionals: Elhanan’s story teaches us about victory over Philistine giants; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Elhanan’s experience of David's mighty men, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
